verdict.rationale: Skyvern's first-party self-hosting docs state that the server runs entirely on your own infrastructure, with your own browsers and LLM keys or a local model, deployable via pip, Docker Compose, or Kubernetes. The GitHub repo, the llms.txt probe ('open-source') and community remarks about the AGPL3 license corroborate that the core is open and self-hostable. The AGPL concern is a licensing preference, not a capability failure. Missing for 10: hands-on independent corroboration of a self-hosted deployment, and documentation of feature parity between self-hosted and cloud (e.g., the CAPTCHA and proxy features).

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can self-host the core product

citations.quote: Self-hosted Skyvern runs entirely on your infrastructure: your servers, your browsers, your LLM API keys.
Run the Skyvern server on your own machine or cluster with pip, Docker Compose, or Kubernetes, using your own LLM keys or a local model.
Run Skyvern on your own infrastructure with your own LLM keys.
